h1: HEIC to JPG Converter — iPhone Photos That Open Everywhere
intro: iPhones save photos as HEIC, which many Windows apps, websites and Android phones can't open. Drop your .heic files here to turn them into normal JPGs — dozens at once, right in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
about:
How to convert HEIC to JPG

  1. Drop your .heic or .heif photos into the box (AirDrop or copy them from your iPhone first).
  2. Keep “JPG” selected — 88% quality looks identical to the original.
  3. Download each photo or all of them as one ZIP.

The first HEIC file loads a small decoder (about 1 MB) once. After that, each photo converts in about a second, even on a phone.

Stop your iPhone saving HEIC

Settings → Camera → Formats → Most Compatible. New photos will be JPG; existing ones stay HEIC, which is what this converter is for.
faq: At 88–92% JPG quality the difference isn't visible. Choose 100% if you want the largest, most faithful file.
Does it keep the photo date and location?
No — the JPG has no EXIF metadata, so date, camera and GPS location are removed. That's safer for sharing; keep the original if you need the date.
The still photo is converted. The short video part of a Live Photo is a separate file and isn't included.

title: JPG to PNG Converter — Free, Batch, No Upload | QuickTiny
desc: Convert JPG photos to PNG in your browser. Batch convert and download as ZIP. Free, private, nothing uploaded.
intro: Need a PNG for an app, a design tool or an upload form? Convert JPG images to PNG here — many at once, entirely on your device.
about:
Good to know

Converting to PNG doesn't add quality or transparency that wasn't in the JPG — it stores the same image in a lossless format, so the file gets bigger. To remove a background, use the background remover.
faq: Why is the PNG so much bigger?
PNG is lossless: it stores every pixel exactly instead of compressing like JPG.
